correctness.rationale: An invariant support simplex would contain antipodal vertices at distance 4, so the realization has a free double cover. The known nine-sphere homotopy type gives simple connectivity and H3 of rank 9. The eight coordinate facets and the even-parity vertices each have the graph on four opposite pairs, with only opposite pairs forbidden. On the parity sphere the involution is the antipodal map. My independent clique recursion, signed-axis cycle calculation and rational Gaussian determinant replay confirmed the face vector (16,80,160,120,16), all nine closed cycles and the specified 25-by-25 determinant -1. The 16 boundaries and nine cycles therefore form a primitive rank-25 lattice in C3; since ker ∂3 has that same rank they generate it over Z. Wedge the inclusion of the projective subspace with the four chosen facet-sphere maps, using paths to the basepoint. The projective summand carries the nontrivial deck generator. On universal covers, its lifted sphere and the two lifts of each of the four facet spheres give precisely the nine generators, up to signs and deck choices. Integral homology Whitehead on the simply connected covers gives the homotopy equivalence downstairs, including the stated torsion and cube of the degree-one mod-two class.
residual_risks: Replay certifies the concrete integral cycle calculation only; the cited nonequivariant theorem and covering-space argument are separate inputs. No extension to other thresholds or groups is inferred.
